question: Which of the following words is mentioned in the preamble of the Indian constitution regarding 'Justice'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Economic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution secures to all citizens JUSTICE — social, economic and political (न्याय — सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक).

• Thus, in the context of 'Justice', the three qualifying words used are social, economic and political; among the given options only Economic appears.

• The idea of social, economic and political justice was drawn from the Russian Revolution (1917) and the objective of a welfare state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Preamble was enacted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

• The Preamble begins with 'We, the People of India' and declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

NOTE

• Secular (Option 1): A word describing the nature of the Indian State (equal treatment of all religions), added by the 42nd Amendment, not linked to 'Justice'.

• Socialist (Option 2): Also added by the 42nd Amendment; describes the economic ideal of the State, not the word used with 'Justice'.

• Sovereign (Option 3): Denotes that India is free from external control; it qualifies the Republic, not 'Justice'.

question: In September 2024, Manish Kumar Gupta has been appointed as Chief Secretary of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In September 2024, senior IAS officer Manish Kumar Gupta was appointed as the Chief Secretary of Arunachal Pradesh (अरुणाचल प्रदेश).

• He is a 1991-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre and took charge in September 2024.

• The Chief Secretary is the administrative head of the state secretariat and the senior-most civil servant of the state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Arunachal Pradesh's capital is Itanagar; it attained full statehood in 1987.

• The Chief Secretary acts as the chief adviser to the Chief Minister and head of the civil services in the state.

• The AGMUT cadre covers Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Mizoram and the Union Territories.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 1): An eastern Indian state with capital Patna; its Chief Secretary is a different officer.

• Manipur (Option 2): A north-eastern state with capital Imphal; not the correct posting here.

• Kerala (Option 3): A southern state with capital Thiruvananthapuram; unrelated to this appointment.

question: In December 2024, as per Ministry of New and Renewable Energy the number of installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana are expected to reach _____ crores by March 2027.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (पीएम सूर्य घर: मुफ्त बिजली योजना), the number of rooftop-solar installations is expected to reach 1 crore by March 2027.

• The scheme aims to provide free electricity to households by installing rooftop solar panels, targeting 1 crore households.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched on 15 February 2024 with an outlay of about ₹75,000 crore.

• It provides up to 300 units of free electricity per month to eligible households.

• Central Financial Assistance (subsidy) is given based on the capacity of the solar system installed.

NOTE

• 5 (Option 1): Overstates the installation target; the goal is 1 crore, not 5 crore.

• 2.5 (Option 3): Not the figure stated for installations under the scheme.

• 3 (Option 4): Refers to the 300 units of free power, not the number of installations in crores.

question: What was India's rank in the Global Innovation Index 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 39th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India was ranked 39th among 133 economies in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2024 (ग्लोबल इनोवेशन इंडेक्स 2024).

• India climbed one position from 40th in 2023 to 39th in 2024, a jump of 42 places since 2015.

• The GII is published annually by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Switzerland topped the GII 2024, followed by Sweden and the United States.

• India was the top-ranked economy among lower-middle-income countries and led the Central and Southern Asia region.

• India is home to a strong startup ecosystem and ranks high in indicators like ICT services exports.

NOTE

• 46th (Option 1): Not India's 2024 rank; India performed better at 39th.

• 19th (Option 2): Too high; no economy of India's income group was placed there for India.

• 61st (Option 3): Reflects an older, lower ranking, not the 2024 position.

question: RBI's Financial Inclusion Index has risen to _____ in 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 67.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The RBI's Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) (वित्तीय समावेशन सूचकांक) rose to 67.0 for March 2025, up from 64.2 in March 2024.

• The index reflects a 4.3% growth across all its sub-components in FY25.

• It measures the extent of financial inclusion across the country on a scale of 0 to 100.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FI-Index was first published by the RBI in 2021 (for the period ending March 2021).

• It is built on three parameters — Access, Usage and Quality — with respective weights of 35%, 45% and 20%.

• A higher value indicates broader and deeper financial inclusion.

NOTE

• 73 (Option 2): Higher than the reported March 2025 value of 67.

• 54 (Option 3): Below the actual figure; corresponds to no reported FI-Index reading for 2025.

• 41 (Option 4): Far below the 2025 value; incorrect for this year.

question: In March 2025, Prime Minister of India laid the foundation stone of National Referral Centre for Wildlife at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Junagadh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 3 March 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of the National Referral Centre for Wildlife (राष्ट्रीय वन्यजीव रेफरल सेंटर) at Junagadh, Gujarat.

• It was done during his visit to the Gir region on World Wildlife Day, where he chaired the 7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife.

• The centre will serve as a hub for wildlife health care, disease diagnosis and referral.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Junagadh in Gujarat is close to Gir National Park, the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion.

• The 7th National Board for Wildlife meeting was held at Sasan Gir.

• India also conducts periodic lion census exercises in the Gir landscape.

NOTE

• Kota (Option 1): A city in Rajasthan known for coaching institutes; not the venue.

• Udaipur (Option 2): The 'City of Lakes' in Rajasthan; unrelated to this centre.

• Bhopal (Option 3): Capital of Madhya Pradesh; not where the foundation was laid.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Gandhi in Champaran', which describes Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha struggle on Indian soil in 1917?
solution_text:
The correct answer is D.G. Tendulkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book 'Gandhi in Champaran' was authored by Dinanath Gopal Tendulkar (डी.जी. तेंदुलकर).

• It describes Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India, the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, against the exploitation of indigo cultivators.

• D.G. Tendulkar is best known for his eight-volume biography of Gandhi titled 'Mahatma'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Champaran Satyagraha (Bihar, 1917) was Gandhi's first major civil disobedience movement in India.

• It targeted the oppressive Tinkathia system under which peasants were forced to grow indigo.

• The movement marked the effective beginning of Gandhi's mass-based struggle in India.

NOTE

• Toru Dutt (Option 1): A 19th-century Indian English poet, author of 'A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields'.

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 2): India's first President; he participated in Champaran but did not write this book.

• Kamala Das (Option 4): A poet and writer known for 'My Story'; unrelated to this work.

question: 'Bhopa', a form of folk music, is traditional to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Bhopa' is a traditional form of folk music and priest-singer tradition of Rajasthan (राजस्थान).

• Bhopas are community bards and priests who sing epic tales of local deities and heroes such as Pabuji.

• They perform using the Ravanhatha (a bowed string instrument) and a long painted scroll called a Phad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The narrative Phad painting tradition is closely linked with Bhopa performances.

• Rajasthan's other folk forms include Maand, Panihari and Ghoomar.

• Manganiyar and Langa are famous folk-musician communities of Rajasthan.

NOTE

• Sikkim (Option 1): A Himalayan state whose folk music is tied to Nepali and Lepcha traditions.

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for Odissi and folk forms like Sambalpuri, not Bhopa.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Associated with Carnatic music and folk forms like Villu Paatu.

question: 'Mohini: The Enchantress' is a mythological fiction authored by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anuja Chandramouli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Mohini: The Enchantress' is a mythological fiction written by Anuja Chandramouli (अनुजा चंद्रमौली).

• The novel retells the story of Mohini, the only female avatar of Lord Vishnu.

• Anuja Chandramouli is a well-known Indian author of mythology-based fiction (पौराणिक कथा).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Her other popular works include 'Arjuna: Saga of a Pandava Warrior-Prince' and 'Kamadeva: The God of Desire'.

• She is often described among India's leading writers of retold Indian mythology.

• Mohini appears in episodes such as the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan).

NOTE

• Shobha Rao (Option 1): An author known for 'Girls Burn Brighter' and 'An Unrestored Woman'.

• Anita Nair (Option 2): Writer of 'Ladies Coupe' and 'Mistress'; not this book's author.

• Deepti Naval (Option 4): An actress and writer known for 'A Country Called Childhood'; unrelated to this novel.

question: 'Jhijhia' dance is related to which of the following Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Jhijhia' is a traditional folk dance of Bihar (बिहार), especially the Mithila region.

• It is performed by women, mainly during the Dussehra/Navratri period, as a prayer to Lord Indra for rain and a good harvest.

• Dancers balance perforated earthen pots with lighted lamps on their heads while dancing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous folk dances of Bihar include Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Paika and Kajari.

• The Mithila region is also renowned for Madhubani painting.

• Jhijhia reflects the agrarian and devotional culture of northern Bihar.

NOTE

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Known for Lavani and Tamasha folk dances.

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Associated with Nati, Kinnauri and Chham dances.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Famous for Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha.

question: The Indian national satellite system (INSAT) program was established in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1983.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian National Satellite System (INSAT) (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय उपग्रह प्रणाली) was established in 1983.

• INSAT is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region.

• The system was commissioned with the launch of INSAT-1B in 1983.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• INSAT serves telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology and search-and-rescue operations.

• It is coordinated by the INSAT Coordination Committee, with ISRO handling the space segment.

• INSAT-1A (1982) failed early, and INSAT-1B (1983) made the system operational.

NOTE

• 1963 (Option 1): The year India launched its first sounding rocket from Thumba, not INSAT.

• 1972 (Option 2): The year the Indian Space Commission and Department of Space were set up.

• 1997 (Option 4): Later period of the INSAT-2 series expansion, not the establishment year.

question: What is the force acting on a unit area of a surface called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pressure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The force acting on a unit area of a surface is called Pressure (दाब).

• Mathematically, Pressure = Force / Area (P = F/A).

• It is a scalar quantity, and its SI unit is the Pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101,325 Pa (1 atmosphere).

• Pressure in fluids increases with depth and acts equally in all directions (Pascal's law).

• Other units of pressure include bar, atm, torr and mmHg.

NOTE

• Force density (Option 1): Refers to force per unit volume, not per unit area.

• Weight (Option 3): The gravitational force on a body (W = mg), measured in newtons.

• Work (Option 4): The product of force and displacement (W = F × d), measured in joules.

question: In January 2025, which organisation has launched a National Mission on Sustainable Packaging Solutions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CSIR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) (सी.एस.आई.आर.) launched a National Mission on Sustainable Packaging Solutions.

• The mission aims to develop eco-friendly, biodegradable and recyclable packaging to reduce plastic waste.

• CSIR is India's largest research and development (R&D) organisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• CSIR was established in 1942 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

• It functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Science and Technology.

• CSIR runs a nationwide network of research laboratories across diverse scientific fields.

NOTE

• IARI (Option 2): The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (Pusa Institute), focused on agricultural research.

• ICAR (Option 3): The Indian Council of Agricultural Research, the apex body for farm research and education.

• DRDO (Option 4): The Defence Research and Development Organisation, focused on military technology.

question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding Public Goods?
option_1: Clothes are an example of Public good.
option_2: It can be provided through the market mechanism.
option_3: It can be provided by the transactions between individual consumers and producers.
option_4: Generally, the benefits of public goods are available to all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Generally, the benefits of public goods are available to all.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A public good (सार्वजनिक वस्तु) is one whose benefits are generally available to all people, and one person's use does not reduce its availability to others.

• Public goods are characterised by non-excludability (no one can be prevented from using them) and non-rivalry (consumption by one does not diminish it for another).

• Examples include national defence, street lighting and public parks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Because of non-excludability, public goods cannot be efficiently provided by the market, leading to the 'free-rider problem'.

• Hence, they are usually provided by the government and financed through taxes.

• Public goods contrast with private goods, which are excludable and rivalrous.

NOTE

• Clothes are an example of Public good (Option 1): Incorrect — clothes are private goods (excludable and rivalrous).

• Provided through the market mechanism (Option 2): Incorrect — the market underprovides public goods.

• Provided by transactions between individual consumers and producers (Option 3): Incorrect — this describes private goods, not public goods.

question: Who were the parents of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shahaji and Jijabai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The parents of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज) were Shahaji Bhonsle (father) and Jijabai (mother).

• Shivaji was born on 19 February 1630 at Shivneri Fort near Pune.

• His mother Jijabai played a key role in shaping his values and leadership.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire and was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674.

• His father Shahaji Bhonsle served the Bijapur Sultanate as a military commander.

• Dadaji Konddev was Shivaji's guardian and administrator, not his father.

NOTE

• Sambhaji and Saibai (Option 2): Sambhaji was Shivaji's son and Saibai was his first wife, not his parents.

• Dada Konddev and Jiiaba (Option 3): Dadaji Konddev was his mentor/guardian, not his father.

• Shahaji and Saiba (Option 4): Names the correct father but wrong mother; his mother was Jijabai.

question: What was the main purpose of the National Renewal Fund?
option_1: To attract foreign direct investment in India.
option_2: To help government for seamless external borrowings.
option_3: To provide assistance to cover the cost of retraining and redeployment of labour.
option_4: To compensate the natural disaster victims.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide assistance to cover the cost of retraining and redeployment of labour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Renewal Fund (NRF) (राष्ट्रीय नवीकरण कोष) was set up in 1992 in the wake of economic liberalisation.

• Its main purpose was to provide assistance to cover the cost of retraining and redeployment of labour affected by industrial restructuring.

• It cushioned workers rendered surplus due to modernisation and closure of sick units.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NRF also funded compensation under the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS).

• It was closely linked to the New Economic Policy (LPG reforms) of 1991.

• The fund aimed to make the social costs of economic reform more manageable.

NOTE

• To attract foreign direct investment (Option 1): FDI is promoted through policy liberalisation, not the NRF.

• To help government for seamless external borrowings (Option 2): External borrowings are managed through other financial mechanisms, not the NRF.

• To compensate natural disaster victims (Option 4): Disaster relief is handled by disaster-response funds, not the NRF.

question: At which of the following places Nana Saheb gathered the armed forces and expelled the British garrison from the city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the Revolt of 1857, Nana Saheb gathered the armed forces and expelled the British garrison from Kanpur (कानपुर).

• Nana Saheb, the adopted son of the last Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the uprising at Kanpur.

• He was aided by his able commander Tatya Tope.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nana Saheb revolted partly because the British denied him the pension under the Doctrine of Lapse.

• The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

• Other centres of the revolt included Delhi (Bahadur Shah Zafar), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai) and Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal).

NOTE

• Delhi (Option 1): Here the rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as emperor, not Nana Saheb's centre.

• Nagpur (Option 2): A Maratha territory annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse, but not Nana Saheb's revolt centre.

• Meerut (Option 3): Where the 1857 revolt first broke out, but the leadership there was of the sepoys, not Nana Saheb.

question: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme was introduced in _____ for issue of Kisan Credit Cards to farmers on the basis of their holdings for uniform adoption by the banks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1998.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme (किसान क्रेडिट कार्ड योजना) was introduced in 1998.

• It provides farmers with timely and adequate credit to meet their agricultural and allied needs.

• The cards are issued on the basis of the farmer's land holdings, for uniform adoption by banks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme was formulated by NABARD on the recommendation of the R.V. Gupta Committee.

• KCC now also covers investment credit for agriculture, animal husbandry and fisheries.

• Loans up to a prescribed limit are eligible for interest subvention under the modified scheme.

NOTE

• 1994 (Option 1): Not the year the KCC scheme was launched.

• 1996 (Option 2): Precedes the KCC scheme's introduction; incorrect.

• 1995 (Option 4): Also earlier than 1998; not the launch year of KCC.

question: Who can dissolve the Indian state Legislative Assembly before its term ends?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Governor (राज्यपाल) can dissolve the state Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) before its term ends.

• This is usually done on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.

• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state under Article 153.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The normal term of a Legislative Assembly is five years unless dissolved sooner.

• The Governor summons, prorogues and dissolves the state legislature under Article 174.

• The Governor is appointed by the President and holds office during the President's pleasure.

NOTE

• Chief Minister (Option 1): Heads the Council of Ministers and advises the Governor, but does not dissolve the Assembly directly.

• Speaker (Option 2): Presides over the Assembly's proceedings but has no power to dissolve it.

• President (Option 4): Can dissolve the Lok Sabha, not a state Legislative Assembly.

question: The Sulaipet and Badampahar mines of Odisha are famous mine for which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron ore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sulaipet and Badampahar mines of Odisha are famous for Iron ore (लौह अयस्क).

• Odisha is India's largest producer of iron ore.

• Badampahar lies in the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other major iron-ore belts of Odisha include Gurumahisani, Kiriburu and Bonai.

• Iron ore in India occurs mainly as haematite and magnetite.

• Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Jharkhand are leading iron-ore producing states.

NOTE

• Dolomite (Option 2): A carbonate mineral used as flux in steel-making; not these mines.

• Limestone (Option 3): Used in cement and steel industries; obtained from different deposits.

• Bauxite (Option 4): The ore of aluminium; Odisha has bauxite reserves at Panchpatmali, not these mines.

question: The inward looking trade strategy followed by Indian in the few initial five year plans is also known as _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Import substitution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inward-looking trade strategy followed by India in the early Five Year Plans is known as Import Substitution (आयात प्रतिस्थापन).

• Its aim was to replace imported goods with domestic production to become self-reliant.

• It relied on protecting domestic industry through high tariffs and import quotas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The strategy is also called Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI).

• It was central to the Second Five Year Plan (Mahalanobis model) emphasising heavy industry.

• The 1991 reforms (LPG) shifted India towards an outward-looking, export-oriented approach.

NOTE

• Export enhancement (Option 1): An outward-looking strategy focused on boosting exports, opposite to import substitution.

• Free trade expansion (Option 2): Involves reducing trade barriers, contrary to the protectionist early plans.

• Foreign investment expansion (Option 4): Emphasises attracting FDI, a feature of the post-1991 open economy.

question: The level of urbanisation in India in 2011 was _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.16%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, the level of urbanisation (शहरीकरण) in India was 31.16%.

• This means about 31% of India's population lived in urban areas in 2011.

• Urbanisation is measured as the proportion of population residing in urban settlements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's total population in Census 2011 was about 121 crore.

• The 2011 Census recorded, for the first time, a larger absolute increase in urban population than rural.

• The most urbanised large states included Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Maharashtra.

NOTE

• 41.16% (Option 2): Overstates the 2011 urbanisation level.

• 21.16% (Option 3): Understates it; closer to earlier decades' figures.

• 45.16% (Option 4): Far higher than the actual 2011 value of 31.16%.

question: What is the primary function of an artificial kidney for humans?
option_2: To remove nitrogenous waste products from the blood
option_3: To filter glucose from the blood
solution_text:
The correct answer is To remove nitrogenous waste products from the blood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary function of an artificial kidney (कृत्रिम वृक्क) is to remove nitrogenous waste products such as urea and creatinine from the blood.

• This process is carried out through haemodialysis, which purifies the blood of patients with kidney failure.

• It works on the principle of diffusion of wastes across a semi-permeable membrane.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dialysis substitutes for the filtering function of the natural kidneys (nephrons).

• The natural kidneys also regulate water, electrolyte balance and blood pressure.

• The functional unit of the kidney is the nephron.

NOTE

• To produce urine (Option 1): Urine formation is a by-product of filtration, not the main purpose of dialysis.

• To filter glucose from the blood (Option 3): Healthy kidneys reabsorb glucose; removing glucose is not the goal.

• To increase blood pressure (Option 4): Dialysis does not aim to raise blood pressure; it removes wastes and excess fluid.

question:
Which of the following organ is part of central nervous system in humans?
I. Heart
II. Spinal cord
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Central Nervous System (CNS) (केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र) in humans consists of the brain and the spinal cord.

• Therefore, among the given options, only the Spinal cord (statement II) is part of the CNS.

• The Heart (statement I) is part of the circulatory system, not the nervous system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The nervous system is divided into the Central Nervous System (CNS) and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS).

• The spinal cord acts as a pathway for signals between the brain and the body and controls reflex actions.

• The brain is protected by the skull, while the spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because the heart belongs to the circulatory system, not the CNS.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since the heart is not part of the central nervous system.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because the spinal cord (II) is indeed part of the CNS.

question: Who authored the treatise 'Arthasastra' that deals primarily with statecraft?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kautilya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The treatise 'Arthasastra' (अर्थशास्त्र) was authored by Kautilya, also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.

• It deals primarily with statecraft, economics, politics and military strategy.

• Kautilya was the chief adviser and minister of Chandragupta Maurya.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Arthashastra is a key source for the history of the Mauryan Empire.

• It advocates a strong, centralised administration and an elaborate system of espionage and taxation.

• The text was rediscovered and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909.

NOTE

• Ashoka (Option 2): The Mauryan emperor famous for his edicts and promotion of Buddhism, not the author.

• Visakhadatta (Option 3): Author of the play 'Mudrarakshasa', which depicts Chanakya but is not the Arthashastra.

• Megasthenes (Option 4): A Greek ambassador who wrote 'Indica', an account of Mauryan India.
